newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds end firm, new issues abound.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds end firm, new issues abound.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds spreads held firm across the maturity spectrum as numerous sought-after new issues stole market attention, dealers said.
"Secondary trading was light as everyone tried to grab a piece of Coke and MedPartners," one dealer said, referring to two new issues which were increased in size due to strong demand.

Coca-Cola Enterprises tapped the primary market for $300 million in A3/AA-minus rated 40-year bonds to yield 6.717 percent or 22 basis points over Treasuries. The issue has a seven-year put option and was managed by Salomon Brothers.
MedPartners Inc followed with $450 million in 10-year Baa3/BBB rated notes priced at 99.156 to yield 7.497 percent or 90 basis points over the 10-year Treasury.
The deal was lead managed by Smith Barney and increased from an originally marketed $300 million in size.
Another sucessful high-grade deal was Morgan Guaranty's $300 million in AA1/AAA rated two-year senior notes, priced at par to yield 6.00 percent via JP Morgan Securities.
A handful of $100 million 144A junk bond deals priced from Specialty Paperboard, Spinnaker Industries, and Rayovac.
